id: title:EDsCODE:allow six hour trino shadow execution

observations.behavior: Changes Trino query execution time limit from 30 minutes (1800s) to six hours (21600s).
observations.posthog_connection: Allows longer-running warehouse queries without premature termination, potentially supporting more complex materialization jobs.

observations.behavior: Increases Temporal workflow start-to-close timeout for Trino-backed workflows from 35 minutes to 365 minutes (~6 hours).
observations.posthog_connection: Supports long-duration data modeling workflows while retaining cancellation safety margins against external dependencies.

observations.behavior: Updates test assertion expectations to match the new 365-minute timeout value.
observations.posthog_connection: Confirms that tests are aligned with the production behavior change regarding Trino-specific timeouts.

observations.limitations: The chunk demonstrates a bounded configuration and implementation change. No broader systemic architecture changes or critical-path dependency resolutions are visible. Documentation updates support but do not independently establish tier 3 impact.

review.limitations: The chunk demonstrates a bounded configuration and implementation change. No broader systemic architecture changes or critical-path dependency resolutions are visible. Documentation updates support but do not independently establish tier 3 impact.
review.reason: This is a substantive, bounded improvement: it extends execution and scheduling limits for warehouse-related workflows. This could prevent false-timeouts during legitimate heavy workloads, improving reliability within this specific subsystem. It does not demonstrate wider architectural risk reduction or cross-component benefits required for tier 3.
review.posthog_relevance: Relevant to PostHog’s managed warehouse ingestion and materialization paths; helps retain jobs that exceed previous short deadlines without dropping them.
review.uncertainty: Assessment relies solely on these hunks; missing context about other workflow dependencies or failure modes prevents higher tier.
